messages.subject: Including categorical variables with interactions
parts:
Hi,

I'm using a spatio-temporal spde model and would like to include fixed effects for a categorical variable (AMP, with four levels: Flinders, Freycinet, Beagle and Huon) and interactions with a continuous variable (year). I initially set this up by creating a model matrix and using expand.factor.strategy = 'model.matrix'. This worked, however I would like estimates for all levels of my factors and the interactions. Therefore, I switched to using expand.factor.strategy = 'inla'. I now get estimates for all factors and interactions, however all my interaction effects have a mean of zero and identical posterior distributions (see below).

Can anyone help with where I am going wrong? When setting up the model matrix manually I had to replace the ":" in the names of the matrix (as suggested in an online tutorial). Might that be the issue here? If so, I'm not sure how to set up the model matrix manually so that it will work with the expand.factor.strategy = 'inla.

TIA

Nick

#Model formula
  inla.spt.form <- z ~ -1 + intercept + AMP*year +
    f(i, model = spde, group = i.group, control.group = list(model = 'ar1', hyper = h.spec))
  
  #Spatio-temporal stack
  stack <- inla.stack(data=list(z=new.dat$count, ntrial=new.dat$ntrial), 
                      A=list(A.t, 1, 1, 1), 
                      effects=list(i.index.t, intercept = rep(1, nrow(new.dat)), AMP = new.dat$AMP, year = new.dat$year))
  
  #fit spatio-temporal model 
  inla.spt.res <- inla(inla.spt.form, data=inla.stack.data(stack), 
                       control.predictor=list(compute = TRUE, A=inla.stack.A(stack)),
                       control.inla=list(int.strategy='eb'),
                       control.compute=list(dic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE, config = TRUE), 
                       control.fixed = list(expand.factor.strategy='inla',
                                            prec = 0.1), 
                       family = "binomial", Ntrials = ntrial)

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Including categorical variables with interactions
parts:
I’m not convinced anything is wrong, but if you want to keep all interaction you easily get some confounding issues, which makes, marginally, effects to be about the same, as only certain contrasts will be likelihood identifiable.  So you might have to define some linear combinations to extract what you want. 

An alternative, is to switch to a sum-to-zero representation, like

> x = as.factor(letters[1:3])
> y = 1:3
> r = inla(y ~ 1 + f(x, model="iid", constr=TRUE, hyper=list(prec=list(initial=0,fixed=T))), data=data.frame(y,x))


So you get the overall mean in the intercept, and then the effects of ‘x’, 3 levels, which sums to zero.


-- 
Håvard Rue
